macro: US equity futures are rallying Monday morning with the S&P up 49 points or 65 basis points, Nasdaq up 329 points or 110 basis points, and the Russell 2000 up 47 basis points. Asian and European markets are broadly higher, with gains of 85-120 basis points across major Eurozone indices and Asia up 1-1.65% across most bourses. The rally is somewhat confounding given a weekend full of negative headlines — escalating Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, a massive Ukrainian drone strike on Russia, and a deluge of bearish AI news — with the primary driver appearing to be diplomatic optimism ahead of this week's UN General Assembly in New York.
rates_fed: Treasuries have a bid this morning with yields down 2-3 basis points across the curve. The Fed remains in hawkish mode — the market is pricing roughly 33 basis points of rate hikes over the final two meetings of the year, with about 50/50 odds of a hike at the October 28th meeting, plus an additional 35 basis points of increases penciled in for 2027. Fed Presidents Schmid and Kashkari both made hawkish remarks recently, warning that elevated inflation is broad-based and not solely an energy story, while Treasury plans to issue over one trillion dollars in T-bills over the next 12 months, pushing short-term debt above 24% of marketable debt.
market_outlook: Adam's lean is cautiously bullish on a session-level basis, driven purely by UN General Assembly diplomatic optimism and the hope that any Middle East progress — however small — could trigger a meaningful drop in oil and a cascade of favorable macro effects. The key catalyst to watch today is any headline out of New York around Trump potentially meeting with Iran's president, as that is the primary fuel behind this morning's risk-on move.
bull_case: The UN General Assembly running September 22-28 brings together leaders from Iran and key Middle East nations, creating a genuine window for diplomatic progress that could send oil prices sharply lower. Even a small geopolitical improvement in the Middle East would have outsized macro benefits — lower yields, reduced inflation, better corporate margins, and improved consumer confidence. Trump reportedly called off Houthi air strikes at the last minute and indicated openness to meeting Iran's president, signaling a de-escalation posture. Additionally, the upcoming Trump-Xi summit on September 24th could yield modest tariff reductions, providing a secondary tailwind.
bear_case: Nearly all the weekend news flow was net negative — Houthis dramatically escalated attacks on Saudi Arabia, Ukraine launched its largest drone strike on Russia hitting oil infrastructure, and a slew of troubling AI headlines emerged including a delayed Anthropic IPO, underwhelming Anthropic revenue projections, massive OpenAI cash burn, and Oracle data center debt problems. The geopolitical situation remains structurally grim with Iran tightening its grip on global energy supply via Hormuz, Iraqi militias, and the Houthis, while oil tanker costs surge and motor oil is being rationed in the US. Monetary policy globally remains hawkish with the BOJ, ECB, and FOMC all hiking this month, and today's rally may simply be wishful thinking about diplomatic breakthroughs that fail to materialize.

tts_summary:
Good morning. Here is your morning game plan for Monday September 21st, 2026.

The macro picture this morning is a tale of two narratives. Futures are rallying — the S&P is up about 49 points, the Nasdaq is up 330 points, and Asia and Europe are broadly green — but the weekend news flow was almost entirely negative. Houthis launched a brazen missile and drone attack on Saudi Arabia. Ukraine hit Russia with its largest drone strike of the war, targeting oil infrastructure. And after Friday's close, a wave of troubling artificial intelligence headlines hit — a delayed Anthropic IPO, disappointing Anthropic revenue projections for 2027, OpenAI burning through cash at an extraordinary rate, and Oracle facing serious debt problems tied to a massive data center in New Mexico.

So why are stocks higher? One word: diplomacy. The United Nations General Assembly kicks off in New York this week, running through September 28th, and markets are betting that some kind of progress can be made on Middle East tensions. Trump reportedly called off Houthi air strikes at the last minute Sunday night, and said he would be open to meeting with Iran's president, who is expected to be in New York. The logic here is straightforward — nearly every macro problem right now traces back to oil. If geopolitical progress were to send energy prices meaningfully lower, you would get a cascade of bullish effects: lower yields, less hawkish monetary policy, better margins, improved consumer confidence. That is the bull case in a nutshell.

The bear case is that this rally is wishful thinking. The geopolitical situation remains structurally dire. Iran is tightening its grip on global energy supply through the Strait of Hormuz, Iraqi militias, and the Houthis. Oil tanker costs are surging. Motor oil is being rationed at US retailers. And monetary policy is still pointed hawkish globally — the Fed, the European Central Bank, and the Bank of Japan all hiked this month, with markets pricing roughly 33 basis points of additional Fed hikes by year-end. Yields are down two to three basis points this morning, but the trend remains upward.

On the company front, a few names to flag. Novo Nordisk is sliding in Europe after disappointing investors at its analyst day by failing to provide granular financial targets — a near-term sentiment negative. Oracle is under pressure from a negative report on debt tied to its Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico, where loan offloading efforts have reportedly hit a wall. On the positive side, Disney's parks business is outperforming peers thanks to smart price promotions and package deals, bucking the industry traffic slump. And Meta has its Connect conference Wednesday night with Zuckerberg delivering the keynote — watch for product announcements as a potential mid-week catalyst.

For the week ahead, the big macro events are the US flash PMIs Wednesday morning and the Trump-Xi summit Thursday. The General Assembly runs all week and any Iran headline — positive or negative — could move markets fast.

Today's calendar is empty of major events. It is a headline-driven session. Stay nimble, watch the oil price, and watch for any Trump-Iran meeting developments out of New York. That is the tape-mover today.
